what_its_for: This combination medicine is used to lower high blood pressure (hypertension). It contains two medicines that work together: olmesartan relaxes and widens your blood vessels, and hydrochlorothiazide (a water pill) helps your kidneys remove extra salt and water from your body. Together, they help lower your blood pressure and reduce your risk of heart attack, stroke, and kidney problems.
how_to_take: Take this medicine by mouth once a day, with or without food. Swallow the tablet whole with a full glass of water. Try to take it at the same time every day so it becomes part of your routine. Do not crush, cut, or chew the tablet unless your doctor tells you it is okay.
dosing: Your doctor will choose the right dose for you based on your blood pressure and how well your body responds to the medicine. Common doses include olmesartan 20 mg/HCTZ 12.5 mg, olmesartan 40 mg/HCTZ 12.5 mg, or olmesartan 40 mg/HCTZ 25 mg taken once daily. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions and never change your dose on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — but only if it is still the same day. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. Call your doctor if you are unsure what to do.
storage: Store this medicine at room temperature between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not use tablets past the expiration date printed on the package.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol, as it can lower your blood pressure too much and cause dizziness or fainting. Do not use salt substitutes or potassium supplements without asking your doctor first, as they can affect your potassium levels. Avoid getting overheated or dehydrated — drink enough fluids, especially in hot weather or during exercise, since the water pill can cause you to lose fluids. Avoid prolonged sun exposure and use sunscreen, as hydrochlorothiazide can make your skin more sensitive to sunlight. Do not take non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) like ibuprofen or naproxen regularly without your doctor's approval, as they can reduce how well this medicine works.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: severe dizziness or fainting; swelling of your face, lips, tongue, or throat (signs of a serious allergic reaction called angioedema); chest pain or rapid heartbeat; signs of low blood pressure such as lightheadedness when standing up; signs of high potassium such as muscle weakness or irregular heartbeat; signs of low potassium such as muscle cramps or weakness; little or no urination, or dark-colored urine; yellowing of the skin or eyes; severe stomach pain, vomiting, or diarrhea; or if you become pregnant, since this medicine can harm an unborn baby.
when_it_works: You may start to see your blood pressure lowering within 1 to 2 weeks of starting this medicine. However, it may take up to 4 to 8 weeks to see the full benefit. Even if you feel well, keep taking the medicine every day. High blood pressure often has no symptoms, so do not stop taking it without talking to your doctor first.
special_populations: Pregnancy: Do NOT use this medicine if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. It can cause serious harm or death to an unborn baby. Use effective birth control while taking this medicine and tell your doctor right away if you become pregnant. Breastfeeding: Talk to your doctor before breastfeeding, as this medicine may pass into breast milk. Elderly patients: Older adults may be more sensitive to dizziness and low blood pressure, especially when standing up. Rise slowly from sitting or lying positions. Kidney or liver disease: Tell your doctor if you have kidney or liver problems, as your dose may need to be adjusted or this medicine may not be right for you. Children: Safety and effectiveness in children under 18 years old has not been established.
